about: Gloomhaven 2nd edition character mats and perk sheets, transcribed from images in C:/Claude/Frosthaven/local/gh2e-data/cards (mats/gh2-<class>.jpeg, perks/gh2-<class>-perks.jpeg) and cross-checked against Gloomhaven Secretariat (C:/Claude/Frosthaven/local/gh2e-data/ghs). Transcribed 2026-10-31.

conventions.icons: Icons are written as words in square brackets: [Attack], [Move], [Range], [Target], [Heal], [Shield], [Retaliate], [Push], [Pull], [Teleport], [Flying], [Loot], [XP], [Damage], [Recover], [Lost], [Spent]; conditions [Stun], [Immobilize], [Disarm], [Muddle], [Wound], [Poison], [Curse], [Bless], [Strengthen], [Invisible], [Ward], [Safeguard]; elements [Fire], [Ice], [Air], [Earth], [Light], [Dark], [Wild] (any element), mixed [Fire/Ice] etc. (one of the two), [X consume] for a consume symbol; items [Body], [Small item]; class symbols such as [Doom], [Tear token], [Plague token], [Supplies], [Prescription], [Song], [Bear], [Command], [Berserker], [Doomstalker].
conventions.modifier_cards: Attack modifier cards are written by their printed value: [+0], [+1], [-1], [-2], [+2], [+3], [+4], [2x] (double), [Null]; [Rolling] is the rolling-modifier symbol; [Shuffle] the reshuffle symbol; "Ignore item [-1] effects" is the black -1 item icon.
conventions.text: Wording, punctuation and curly quotes are kept as printed; card names in italics on the sheet are plain text here.
conventions.boxes: boxes = number of check boxes beside the perk; linked = the boxes are drawn as one tall box with dashed dividers (all must be checked to gain the perk once). Every sheet has 18 perk boxes and a perk-mark track of 6 x 3 check marks.
conventions.hp: hp = maximum hit points at levels 1-9 from the mat's level track.

class_notes: You are a strong, melee fighter with a large pool of hit points. But if you run into the fray without using any defensive abilities, you may find yourself near death quite quickly. Fortunately, you have a number of tools to help reduce incoming damage. If you intend on using more offensive abilities, you may need to pick your spots to attack from more carefully to avoid taking too many hits.

You have many powerful melee attack abilities with an area of effect that are great when enemies clump up for you. When you can’t naturally find groups of enemies next to each other, you also have a variety of abilities that [Push] or [Pull] to move the enemies into place.

class_notes: You are versatile and can fill the needs of your party with a variety of offensive and healing abilities. Communicating with your allies when choosing your ability cards for the scenario can make everyone more effective together.
You’re a bit slow to get around. With limited access to big moves and fast initiatives, try to plan ahead.

You have the ability to throw rocks around the battlefield. Not only do you get bonuses directly from creating or moving the obstacles, you can also use them to slow down enemies approaching your party.
There is no limit to the number of obstacles you can place, just remember that whenever you’re creating or moving them, you cannot completely cut off any section of the map.

class_notes: You have key actions known as Augments [Augment]. When you perform an augment ability, you place that card in your active area to gain a persistent bonus on your melee attacks. You may only have one augment active at a time; if you perform a second augment ability, you must discard the previous active augment. Augment abilities are mandatory, so you must switch to the new augment if you want to perform any other abilities from that action.

As a class with few hit points who spends a significant amount of time close to enemies, carefully avoiding enemy focus is integral to your success. You have access to fast and slow initiatives, allowing you to dance in and out of combat by approaching enemies late in the round and then getting away from them early the following round. Additionally, you can disable threatening enemies with your abilities that [Immobilize], [Disarm], or [Stun]. You can even become [Invisible] when in dangerous situations.

class_notes: Rather than fighting with pure brute force, you have two tactics to gain the upper hand in combat: attacking enemies who are distracted by your adjacent allies or attacking enemies who are completely isolated on the battlefield. Understanding how your allies move and communicating with them regarding their plans can help you determine which approach is best for you both before and during a scenario.

Because of your small hand size, losing cards has a steep cost. If you find yourself often exhausted well before the end of the scenario, you may gain more turns by performing fewer actions with [Lost] early on.

It is easy for you to go early in the round, but you may also want to bring some cards with late initiatives to allow you to approach enemies after their turns, allowing you to get free attacks safely.

class_notes: As you have a very small hand size, the top action of Reviving Ether is an essential tool for your longevity. Be careful not to lose this card when performing a short rest or to negate a source of damage. Additionally, as you will typically want to play it when most of your cards are in your lost pile, you may need to be especially cautious with your positioning when preparing for it.

Despite your hand size, a significant portion of your power comes from performing actions with [Lost]. While Reviving Ether will gain you a significant amount of stamina, you may still exhaust earlier than you would like if you lose too many cards in quick succession. As a starting point, if you perform one action with [Lost] between each of your rests, you should have a reasonable number of turns.

class_notes: You have the right tool for any job: whether an ally needs some healing, you want to set enemies up with some well-placed traps, or you want to take a more direct approach with something a bit more explosive.

Your large hand size gives you a significant amount of stamina, allowing you to play more cards with [Lost] than other classes typically would. However, if you lose too many cards too early in a scenario, you may find yourself exhausted before the end.

Some of your abilities let you place unique tokens on the map that have varying effects. Unlike traps, hexes containing one or more of these tokens are still empty and are not considered negative hexes for the purposes of monster movement.

class_notes: You live life on the edge, skirting the line between life and death. Many of your abilities let you spend your hit points to increase their power. Accordingly, you may often need to view your hit point value as a resource. Additionally, many of your abilities are stronger when your current hit point value is half your maximum hit point value or less. Your survival will depend on your ability to determine when to spend hit points, when to keep your hit point value low, and when to heal up to safety.

You have a number of very powerful actions with [Lost]. While many may seem very tempting, you also have a small hand size, meaning you may want to be selective with which ones you use to avoid exhausting too early. If you decide to go all-in, make sure your party is ready to keep up.

class_notes: You are the master of elements. While others use more mundane instruments, your weapons are the elements themselves. You can do almost anything if you have the appropriate element. Conversely, when all elements are inert, your powers are rather meager. As such, planning a turn or two ahead will be paramount. While doing so, it’s important to identify when being at your strongest is most valuable to your party based on your circumstances.

You have a number of actions and attack modifiers that infuse mixed or wild elements. Whenever performing one of these infusions, note that you choose which element you are infusing at the end of that turn, when you move that element to the strong column.

class_notes: You start each scenario with [Invisible] and do not lose [Invisible] at the end of your turns. While you are [Invisible], you cannot perform attack abilities or open doors, you may move through enemies as if they were your allies, and enemies treat the hex you occupy as unoccupied. If an enemy ends its movement in your hex, you must [Teleport] to the closest empty hex and suffer hazardous terrain damage. When all other characters are exhausted or have escaped, you lose [Invisible] and cannot gain it.

You can also place Tear Tokens [Tear token] on the map. Hexes with only [Tear token] in them are empty and not negative. You may place a maximum of two [Tear token] at any time (you may remove one to replace it elsewhere). Whenever you enter a hex containing a [Tear token] during an ability, you may remove the [Tear token] to lose [Invisible] at the end of the ability. At the end of each round in which you perform an attack, gain [Invisible]. Some of your abilities have [Tear hex] hexes. When you perform the ability, you may place one [Tear token] in that hex.

class_notes: You enjoy nothing more than spreading Xorn’s gifts of poison and plague with those near you. You have abilities that give enemies Plague Tokens [Plague token]. [Plague token] are not negative conditions, have no innate effects, and cannot be removed by enemies. You have access to 12 [Plague token] and if you would ever give an enemy an 13th [Plague token], you must first remove any one previously-placed [Plague token]. An enemy may have up to 3 [Plague token].

Xorn loves your friends and foes equally. Many of your abilities can be augmented by applying [Poison] to allies. You may only activate these conditional bonuses if you can give [Poison] to an ally who does not already have [Poison]. You have a variety of effects that specifically benefit allies that have [Poison], so your allies will also come to embrace the [Poison] you so kindly share with them.

class_notes: Many of your abilities allow you to gather Supplies [Supplies], which are used to recover your and your allies’ [Lost] and [Spent] items. When you gain [Supplies], move the Supplies token [Supplies] up the track. You start each scenario with 10 [Supplies] and may have up to 50. When you spend Supplies [Spend supplies], set the track to 0; then you may [Recover] any number of the target’s items with a combined gold cost equal to or less than the amount of [Supplies] spent. You must have at least 10 [Supplies] to perform an ability or added effect that requires spending them.

You have a special personal supply of [Quartermaster] items. They are not immediately brought into scenarios but can be given to characters through your abilities. These items have no item slot requirements and may be used by characters regardless of their equipped items. There is only one copy of each [Quartermaster] item card—if any character already has that item, you may not give out another copy. When a [Quartermaster] item is used, it is returned to its supply. At the end of each scenario, unused [Quartermaster] items are returned to their supply.

back.title: Valrath Quartermaster
lore: Valraths originate far in the south of Casskia, in the Red Desert. There was once a great war in that region between Valraths and the humans, both equally interested in conquering the Stormbrew Plains for themselves. The two nations have since made peace, and the Valrath government in particular has made concerted efforts to forsake its aggressive past. In more recent times, they have focused on economic strength over physical domination.

This economic strength can take many forms. Valraths have a strong presence in the Merchant’s Guild, though many prefer to establish more independent business ventures. One could say Quartermasters are a form of merchant, maintaining a stock of goods to keep a fighting force equipped and prepared. That fighting force may be a city garrison or a small mercenary band. For the right price, a Quartermaster can make sure anyone has a good sword at their side for when they need it most.

class_notes: You have abilities that can give character allies medical packs, which are extra ability cards. When someone gains a medical pack, add one random card from medical pack supply directly to their hand. Abilities that give medical packs may only be performed if there is at least one medical pack remaining in the supply. Medical packs that have been added to someone’s hand can be played during card selection like any other ability card. Once an action on a medical pack has been performed or the medical pack is otherwise discarded, return that card to your medical pack supply. A player may not lose a medical pack to negate a source of damage.

You also have Prescription [Prescription] actions, which can only be performed if you have at least one adjacent character ally. class_notes: Many of your actions have one of two notes associated with them: high notes [High note] or low notes [Low note]. Once each round, when you perform an action with a note, you may immediately gain the corresponding note token and place it to the left. You may have a maximum of two of each note at once and you start each scenario with one note of your choice.

You may play notes to create Songs [Song], which are persistent active abilities with use slots that provide ongoing effects. In order to perform a [Song], you must have the corresponding notes on your mat. Whenever you perform a [Song], remove all of your notes, even those that were not part of the [Song]. The [Song]’s effect is active from the moment you play it into your active area and ends when the [Song] is moved from your active area to your discard pile. You must advance your character token on all your active [Song] at the end of each round. If multiple [Song] have effects at the end of your turn, you may apply their effects in any order.

back.title: Quatryl Soothsinger
lore: Quatryls typically don’t like being underestimated. Yes, they are smaller than the other ancestries they encounter, but that doesn’t mean they are worth any less. If anything, they will go out of their way to show they are worth more. Their scientific institutions on the eastern continent have developed a myriad of technological advancements—primarily bionics and prosthetics used to enhance their own capabilities. Only a fool would shun a Quatryl’s offer of help.

The talents of a Quatryl can extend far beyond the realms of machinery and alchemy. Their long, deft fingers also facilitate astonishing capabilities with musical instruments, given the proper training. Combining this with a Quatryl’s distinctive vocal traits makes their musical talents go far beyond merely entertaining crowds. Soothsingers have been known to empower their allies to great feats and bring their enemies low with a single strum of their lute and the proper note in their voice.

class_notes: You start every scenario with your bear summon [Bear] by summoning it in an empty adjacent hex before the first round. Its stats are listed below, and it acts immediately before you each round. You may lose cards as normal to negate damage done to you or [Bear]. If [Bear] drops below 1 hit point, it is removed from the map and cannot return that scenario. You have special actions known as Command [Command] actions that grant [Bear] additional abilities, ignoring your line-of-sight. [Bear] will not open doors during its turn, but you may [Command] it to open doors.

Some of your actions require an element in order to be performed. You cannot perform those actions without using the indicated element. You may sometimes have multiple persistent abilities that trigger at the same time. When that happens, you choose the resolution order.
